commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MoE] Fix gfx950 block scale swizzle for AITER Triton MXFP4 W4A16
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

The AITER Triton MXFP4 W4A16 backend crashes the process on gfx950 (MI355) with a
GPU memory access fault, because it tells the kernel its block scales are not
swizzled while weight loading has already swizzled them. This passes the existing
CDNA4 swizzle gate through to the kernel, which makes the path work on gfx950.

## The failure

Failing test: 
`tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle[16-256-256-8-4-AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_BF16]`

CI failure: [AMD CI #12514](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12514/list?jid=01a05c92-2f80-48ef-9509-81f3c2ff0de5&tab=output)

ROCm names the faulting kernel directly in the runtime message: aiter's Triton
`moe_gemm_a16w4`, entered on the first of the two GEMM calls in the expert
forward pass.

## Root cause

On gfx950 with TP <= 2, `_swizzle_mxfp4` stores the mxfp4 block scales in the
CDNA4 swizzled layout at weight load time. The kernel has to be told, and the
gate that decides this is shared: the docstring of
`should_use_cdna4_mx_scale_swizzle` states that the load-time swizzle and the
kernel argument must agree.

The a8w4 sibling path does agree, it passes `swizzle_mx_scale=swz`. The a16w4
path introduced in [#50622](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50622)
hardcoded `swizzle_mx_scale=None` at both of its GEMM call sites, so the kernel
indexed a swizzled scale buffer as if it were linear and walked off the end of
the allocation.

This is also why the original validation looked clean: it was run on MI300X
(gfx942), where the gate is false and no swizzle is applied, so `None` was the
correct value there. Only gfx950 swizzles, and only gfx950 faults.

## The fix

Compute the same gate the a8w4 path uses and pass it to both `moe_gemm_a16w4`
calls. When the gate is false non-gfx950, or TP >= 4 where the CDNA4 layout is
not used, the value stays `None` exactly as before, so gfx942 and gfx1250 keep
their current behaviour.

## Test results

Hardware: AMD MI355X (gfx950). 
12 passed and 0 skipped

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Bound recursive argument parsers
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #50927.

Gemma4 argument parsing and MiniMax M3 parameter parsing contain hand-written recursive grammars. Deeply nested model output can exhaust a worker thread stack and terminate the process.

This change adds a shared thread-local RAII guard with a maximum of 128 active recursive parser frames. Gemma4 enters the guard after recognizing an object or array opener, and MiniMax M3 enters it after recognizing an element opener. The guard returns a cut error at the limit and restores the previous depth on normal return, parse errors, and unwinding. Its thread-bound marker keeps increment and restoration on the same thread.

The parser audit found these as the two hand-written recursive model-output parsing paths in the Rust parser crate. JSON parsing continues to use serde_json's built-in recursion limit.

Related: #50944.

## Test Plan

- cargo test -p vllm-parser
- cargo clippy -p vllm-parser --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- git diff --check

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Log platform plugin detection failures
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Addresses the diagnostic failure described in #52238.

Platform discovery currently discards exceptions raised by platform plugins.
On an AMD Zen CPU, an `OSError` while loading an incompatible zentorch shared
library therefore causes the CPU plugin to be dropped and leaves vLLM on
`UnspecifiedPlatform`, without exposing the underlying failure even at DEBUG
level.

Rather than treating every zentorch import failure as safe to recover from,
this change logs exceptions from failed platform probes at DEBUG level with
their traceback. `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` will now surface the plugin name and
the original loading error without continuing from a potentially partially
initialized zentorch import.

A regression test simulates the reported zentorch `OSError` and verifies that
platform discovery logs both the failed CPU plugin and the original exception.

I reviewed the issue comments and searched open PRs for both `#52238` and
platform-plugin exception logging. No overlapping open PR was found.

AI assistance was used to develop and test this change. I reviewed every
changed line and understand and can defend the change end-to-end.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/platforms/__init__.py tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor skip_decoder_start_token in async encoder-decoder rendering
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Make asynchronous encoder-decoder rendering honor the multimodal processor's
`skip_decoder_start_token` policy, matching the existing synchronous path.

`EncDecMultiModalProcessor` uses this flag when a processor already supplies a
complete decoder prefix. The synchronous renderer passes the flag to
`build_enc_dec_input`, but `_process_enc_dec_async` omitted it and therefore
used the default value of `False`.

This bug is exercised by the normal online transcription path:

```text
/v1/audio/transcriptions
  -> speech-to-text preprocessing
  -> render_cmpl_async()
  -> _process_enc_dec_async()
  -> build_enc_dec_input()
```

Cohere ASR sets `skip_decoder_start_token = True`, so every Cohere ASR
transcription request enters the affected path. For long audio, preprocessing
splits the input into chunks and each chunk independently passes through the
same async renderer path.

With `CohereLabs/cohere-transcribe-03-2026`, the correct 10-token decoder prefix
is:

```text
[13764, 7, 4, 16, 62, 62, 5, 9, 11, 13]
```

Before this change, the async path incorrectly prepended BOS token `4`, making
the decoder prompt 11 tokens long:

```text
[4, 13764, 7, 4, 16, 62, 62, 5, 9, 11, 13]
```

This is a deterministic decoder-input error. The extra token changes decoder
positions, self-attention state, and the model probability distribution, and it
adds one decoder prefill token per request or audio chunk. It does not imply
that the final greedy transcript will visibly change for every audio sample.

This PR extracts the existing policy lookup into a shared helper and uses it in
both synchronous and asynchronous encoder-decoder rendering. Behavior remains
unchanged for Whisper and other processors that keep the default value of
`False`, as well as renderers without an encoder-decoder multimodal processor.

## Test Plan

Focused renderer tests:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/inputs/test_preprocess.py \
  tests/renderers/test_completions.py -q
```

Lint and static checks:

```bash
python -m pre_commit run \
  --files vllm/renderers/base.py
```

The real Cohere ASR renderer was also exercised with the model processor,
tokenizer, and demo WAV from `CohereLabs/cohere-transcribe-03-2026`. A V1
`AsyncLLM` A/B run compared the fixed 10-token decoder prompt with the previous
behavior simulated by prepending BOS.

## Test Result

Focused renderer tests:

```text
37 passed, 14 warnings in 7.81s
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

The real Cohere ASR renderer produced the expected result:

| Path | Decoder prompt length | Decoder prompt prefix |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Fixed async path | 10 | `[13764, 7, 4, 16, 62, 62, 5, 9, 11, 13]` |
| Previous async behavior | 11 | `[4, 13764, 7, 4, 16, 62, 62, 5, 9, 11, 13]` |

On an NVIDIA A100 40 GB using BF16 and greedy decoding, five audio variants
(full, first half, second half, reduced amplitude, and silence) completed in
both A/B cases. The first-token
log probability for the full sample changed:

| Decoder input | First generated token | Log probability |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Fixed 10-token prefix | `If` (1617) | -0.0413764976 |
| Previous behavior with BOS | `If` (1617) | -0.0406677909 |

This confirms that the bug deterministically changes the online decoder input.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Restore the chat template content format mismatch warning
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`resolve_chat_template_content_format` returns an explicitly specified
`--chat-template-content-format` without ever comparing it against the format
detected from the template. The warning that was written to catch exactly that
mismatch has been unreachable since #19735.

## Root cause

#19735 added an early return so that a specified format skips the Jinja AST
parse:

```diff
+    if given_format != "auto":
+        return given_format
...
-    return detected_format if given_format == "auto" else given_format
+    return detected_format
```

Detection also fed `_log_chat_template_content_format`, which has exactly one
caller — below that early return. So the forced path exits before the logger,
and the logger is only ever reached when `given_format == "auto"`. The guard

```python
if given_format != "auto" and given_format != detected_format:
```

is false on every reachable path. `git log -S` puts this at #19735 (June 2025).

## Impact

Forcing a format the template cannot consume fails in one of two ways. Running
vLLM's own detection helpers over the 35 templates in `examples/` (33 usable):

| forced format | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | correct on every template |
| `string` | correct on every template |
| `openai` | 17 raise `TypeError`, 8 silently corrupt, 8 fine |

The 17 concatenate with `+` and raise `can only concatenate str (not "list") to
str`, surfacing as HTTP 500. The other 8 interpolate with `{{ message.content }}`,
so Jinja calls `str()` on the list and renders the Python repr into the prompt:

```
### Instruction:
[{'type': 'text', 'text': 'Reply with exactly OK.'}]
```

HTTP 200, no exception, nothing in the logs. For those 8 templates
(`alpaca`, `inkbot`, `teleflm`, `llama3.2_pythonic`, `phi4_mini`, `toolace`,
`xlam_llama`, `xlam_qwen`) this warning is the only signal in the system.

## Changes

- Restore detection before the return and select with a ternary, as the code did
  prior to #19735. The override still wins; only the comparison is added back.
- Gate the info line on `auto`, so users who already passed the flag are not told
  they can pass it to override.
- Cache the resolved content format, so restoring detection does not add
  per-request work (see below).
- Inline the logging and use `info_once` / `warning_once`, removing
  `_log_chat_template_content_format`.

## Test

Verified against `examples/template_chatml.jinja` (detected `string`) and
`tool_chat_template_llama3.1_json.jinja` (detected `openai`):

| template | given | returned | logged |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| chatml | `openai` | `openai` | warning |
| chatml | `string` | `string` | — |
| llama3.1 | `openai` | `openai` | — |
| chatml | `auto` | `string` | info |

The override is honoured in every case and only the genuine mismatch warns.

`pytest tests/renderers/test_hf.py` gives 28 passed with the existing
content-format tests unaffected. The 3 failures (`ultravox`,
`Llama-Guard-3-1B`, `paligemma-3b-mix-224`) are `403 Cannot access gated repo`
and reproduce identically on a clean tree. Built and run from source on Apple
Silicon (CPU backend, Python 3.12); `pre-commit run` passes.

## Notes for reviewers

- **This does not close #54486.** That issue asks for the combination to be
  rejected before request handling; this only restores the diagnostic. Filing it
  as the symptom that surfaced the regression.
- **Performance.** Detection now runs even when a format is given, so per
  review it is cached. `lru_cache` was not usable — `tools` is a list and
  `ModelConfig` sets `__eq__` without `__hash__` — so this follows the existing
  `_PROCESSOR_CHAT_TEMPLATES` idiom and keys a bounded dict on the fields that
  select the template. Only the presence of `tools` is in the key: it decides
  whether the processor template is tried, and its contents never reach the AST.
  The bound matters because a request can carry its own `chat_template`.

  Measured on Qwen2-VL-2B, explicit chat template: **~16 us -> 0.109 us** per
  call once warm. With `chat_template=None` it was already ~0.2 us, since
  `_try_get_processor_chat_template` and `_detect_content_format` are memoized;
  the cost sat in `tokenizer.get_chat_template()` on the explicit path. Detected
  format is unchanged against an uncached resolve for all 35 templates in
  `examples/`.

- **Eight advisory warnings.** Forcing `string` on a template that also supports
  `openai` renders correctly but still warns, since the formats differ. That
  seems right — you have silently given up multimodal capability — and the
  warning's own text is advisory. Happy to narrow it to the
  `detected == "string"` direction if preferred.
- **Overlap with #53824.** That PR touches the same two files but a different
  function (`_iter_nodes_assign_content_item`, improving detection accuracy).
  Complementary rather than duplicate — it makes detection more correct, this
  makes a wrong override visible — but there may be a textual conflict in the
  test file depending on merge order.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed
line, and the test results above were run locally. The commit carries a
`Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

## Purpose

Fixes #47137

When generation terminates (`max_tokens`/`length` or a `stop` string) inside a `<tool_call>` opener that has not been promoted to a tool call, the streaming path drops the buffered markup but the non-streaming path returned it as `content` — the two paths disagreed for identical model output.

Contrary to the hope in the issue thread that #46875 had fixed this, I re-ran the issue's no-server unit reproduction on current main (`978de83`) and **the divergence still reproduces** (confirming @TheDuyIT's July 1 retest):

```
2 '<tool_call>\n'          stream= ''  nonstream= '<tool_call>\n'   DIVERGE
3 '<tool_call>\n<'         stream= ''  nonstream= '<tool_call>\n<'  DIVERGE
4 '<tool_call>\n<function' stream= ''  nonstream= '<tool_call>\n<function' DIVERGE
```

Root cause: in `DelegatingParser._extract_tool_calls`, the no-tool-calls branch returned the raw `content` instead of `tool_call_info.content` — the tool parser's cleaned content, which already strips incomplete tool-call markup while preserving any real content generated before the opener. This is "Direction B" from the issue, matching @bbrowning's stated expected behavior ("non-streaming should now match streaming and drop the incomplete markup until we have a valid tool call").

## Changes

- `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`: the auto-tool-choice no-tool-calls branch now returns the tool parser's content (scoped to engine-based parsers per review).
- `vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py`: deferred-content flush keeps original text order around unpromoted tool blocks (review round 2, patch by @TheDuyIT).
- `vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py` + `adapters.py`: `skip_reasoning_parsing` flag so tool parsers pass reasoning markup through verbatim when no reasoning parser is configured (review round 3, reported by @TheDuyIT).
- `vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py`: the bypass derives its terminal set from the config's transition table instead of the `THINK_START`/`THINK_END` labels — a marker qualifies only if all its transitions stay within CONTENT/REASONING and emit only reasoning events, and one shared marker disables the bypass for the whole config. Inkling (whose `<|end_message|>` carries the `THINK_END` label but closes every block kind) computes an empty set and parses unchanged; `<think>`-style configs still compute `{THINK_START, THINK_END}` (review round 4, reported by @bbrowning).
- `tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py`: regression tests for all of the above — truncated-opener parity cases, content-order preservation, think-markup passthrough for both engine failure modes, and sanity checks that complete tool calls still promote.
- `tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py`: inkling tool parser with no reasoning parser — plain text, tool blocks, and thinking blocks in both paths, plus an engine-level test that the flag is inert for shared markers (7 of the 11 fail on the previous head).

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

The issue timeline has no cross-referenced PRs and `gh pr list --search "47137"` returns none (checked immediately before opening). @IMvision12 and @Kronten28 expressed interest in the thread (Jun 30 / Jul 1) but no PR was opened in the days since, and the thread stalled on the open question of whether the bug still exists — which the reproduction above settles.

## Test Plan

As of 4b5d6bd890 (current merge state with `main`):

```
$ pytest tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py -k "TruncatedToolOpener or ThinkMarkup" -v
10 passed

$ pytest tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py
96 passed

$ pytest tests/parser/ --ignore=tests/parser/mistral
3931 passed

$ pytest tests/tool_parsers/ --ignore=tests/tool_parsers/test_cohere_command_tool_parser.py
968 passed, 3 skipped, 34 xfailed

$ pre-commit run --files <changed files>
ruff check / ruff format / typos / mypy: Passed
```

The two ignores are local-environment issues that reproduce identically on current `main` without this PR: `tests/parser/mistral/` fails on a `mistral_common` version skew (`GrammarFactory.select_jinja_template()` signature) and the cohere test module needs the optional `cohere_melody` package.

Also re-ran the issue's part-D reproduction with the fix: all three truncation points now MATCH between streaming and non-streaming.

## Test Result

All new and existing parser tests pass on macOS CPU (editable install, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`).

---

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector] Support heterogeneous TP sharing in Mooncake Store Connector
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR allows vLLM instances using the same backend-native LBHNC or LBNHC
layout, whose TP sizes divide a common Store TP size, to share the same KV
cache through Mooncake Store. Sharing vLLM instances must use the same PP size
and satisfy the KV-head and topology requirements described below.

Previously, Mooncake Store keys and physical data layouts were tied to the
local TP rank. Even when Prefill and Decode instances used the same model,
different TP sizes produced different Store shard counts, KV-head ranges, and
key namespaces, so the instances could not hit the same KV cache entries.

This PR introduces a fixed Store TP layout that decouples Store objects from
the local TP size of a vLLM instance:

- `store_tp_size` defines a stable number of logical Store shards;
- for regular MHA/GQA sharing, each Store shard contains a fixed range of
  global KV heads;
- one local TP rank maps to one or more consecutive Store shards;
- vLLM instances with different local TP sizes can read and write the same key
  namespace when they use the same native KV layout and Store TP size;
- a Decode consumer with `save_decode_cache` enabled writes newly completed
  decode KV blocks back in the same Store TP layout.

The implementation separates logical token enumeration from the Store payload
layout:

- `ChunkedTokenDatabase` enumerates logical token chunks and their hashes;
- `StoreLayout` defines Store keys, required lookup shards, local buffer spans,
  and KV-cache tensor registration and validation;
- the transfer workers execute layout-provided Store operations without
  model- or layout-specific branches.

`RankLocalStoreLayout` preserves the existing rank-local format, while
`LBHNCStoreLayout` and `LBNHCStoreLayout` implement the common Store TP shard
formats used by this PR.

For example, with Store TP size 4:

- each TP4 rank maps to one Store shard;
- each TP2 rank maps to two Store shards;
- KV written by a TP4 Prefill instance can be read by a TP2 Decode instance;
- KV written back by the TP2 Decode instance can be reused by compatible TP4
  or TP2 instances.

The Store layout follows the attention backend's resolved LBHNC
(`[layers, blocks, KV heads, tokens, head size]`) or LBNHC
(`[layers, blocks, tokens, KV heads, head size]`) layout. LBHNC uses contiguous
head ranges directly. LBNHC represents each shard as token-wise head ranges
through Mooncake multi-buffer I/O. Neither path changes the attention
backend's selected layout or requires a layout-conversion staging buffer.
Because the layout is encoded in the Store namespace, LBHNC and LBNHC
endpoints use separate Store entries rather than reading each other's payloads.

Deployments with multiple Prefill TP sizes can explicitly select a common
Store TP size:

```json
{
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
        "enable_store_tp_lcm": true,
        "prefill_tp_sizes": [4, 2]
    }
}
```

When `enable_store_tp_lcm` is enabled, the connector uses the least common
multiple of `prefill_tp_sizes` as the common Store TP size. For example, the
least common multiple of 4 and 2 is 4, so the configuration above selects
Store TP size 4. This selection does not change the runtime TP size of any
vLLM instance.

All Prefill and Decode instances sharing the namespace calculate the same
Store TP size from the same configuration. Decode does not inspect which
Prefill TP size produced an individual request and does not change its write
layout per request. With Prefill TP sizes 4 and 2 and Decode TP size 2, all
using the same supported KV layout:

- each TP4 Prefill rank writes one Store shard;
- each TP2 Prefill rank writes two Store shards;
- each TP2 Decode rank reads and writes two Store shards.

Decode therefore writes according to the common Store TP size, rather than its
own local TP size or the TP size of a particular Prefill instance. Its local KV
heads are mapped back to the same global Store shards, so decode KV written by
one compatible topology remains reusable by the others.

When automatic common Store TP size selection is not enabled, all vLLM
instances use the explicitly configured `store_tp_size` and follow the same
mapping rules.

The vLLM instances must already satisfy the existing Mooncake Store
compatibility requirements (same model/KV format, block and hash
configuration, and cache namespace). Heterogeneous-TP sharing additionally
requires:

- all sharing endpoints use the same LBHNC or LBNHC KV cache layout;
- Store TP size is greater than or equal to local TP size;
- Store TP size is divisible by local TP size;
- for MHA/GQA, the model's total number of KV heads is divisible by Store TP
  size; MQA (`Hkv == 1`) uses a replicated shared layout instead;
- all sharing vLLM instances use the same PP size;
- the KV cache contains one Full Attention group;
- PCP and DCP are not used.

Different local TP sizes give each rank a different number of KV heads. This
implementation first divides the model's global KV heads into fixed Store
shards and then maps each local rank's KV heads to one or more consecutive
Store shards. MQA is handled separately: because every TP rank holds the same
single KV head, it uses a replicated shared layout instead of regular
Store-head partitioning.

vLLM instances with different PP sizes do not share a Store namespace. The PP
size is encoded in the namespace, preventing incompatible PP topologies from
hitting each other's KV cache entries. The KV layout is also encoded, so
LBHNC and LBNHC instances remain isolated from each other.

If any sharing condition is not satisfied, the connector falls back to an
isolated rank-local namespace that includes the local TP, PP, and KV layout.

This PR also updates the Mooncake Store Connector documentation and adds
regression coverage for:

- LBHNC and LBNHC Store-shard mapping and round trips across different TP
  sizes;
- vLLM instances whose ranks hold different numbers of KV heads;
- layout-specific shared Store key namespaces;
- common Store TP size selection for multiple Prefill TP sizes;
- PP namespace isolation;
- rank-local fallback for unsupported layouts, malformed configurations, and
  incompatible topologies;
- the shared MQA namespace;
- logical-block KV event aggregation for multi-shard Store writes, including
  partial shard failures and mixed existing/missing shards;
- replication-aware KV event aggregation for GQA and MQA TP striping.

## Related Issues and PRs

- Issue #45036 tracks the Mooncake Store Connector roadmap and lists
  "Decode-Phase KV Cache Put with GQA TP Asymmetry" as an open item. This PR
  covers the Full Attention case where TP sizes are divisible, PP sizes match,
  and KV heads can be partitioned by a common Store TP size.
- PR #36869 added heterogeneous-TP support to `MooncakeConnector` for direct
  P/D KV transfer. In contrast, this PR targets `MooncakeStoreConnector`, where
  KV is persisted using a stable Store-shard layout and can be reused and
  updated by multiple Prefill and Decode instances.
- PR #52466 added Decode KV offloading to Mooncake Store consumers. This PR
  extends that path so Prefill and Decode instances with different TP sizes can
  read and write the same KV cache using a common Store TP size.
- PR #52516 fixes heterogeneous-TP mapping in `MooncakeConnector` when TP size
  exceeds the number of KV heads and the heads are replicated. This PR uses a
  separate Store-shard mapping and limits regular sharing to topologies where
  the total number of KV heads is divisible by Store TP size. Unsupported
  topologies fall back to an isolated rank-local namespace.

## Test Plan

### Unit and static checks

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  docs/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage.md \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_layout.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/connector.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/data.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_layout.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py
```

### RDMA cluster tests

Reusable E2E test code:

- [Heterogeneous-TP cluster test directory](https://github.com/ScaleX-IO/vllm/tree/14d0dd92ad/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store_connector/heterogeneous_tp_cluster)
- [Single-node RDMA layout matrix](https://github.com/ScaleX-IO/vllm/blob/14d0dd92ad/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store_connector/heterogeneous_tp_cluster/run_single_node_rdma_layout_matrix.sh)
- [Multiple-Prefill-TP correctness runner](https://github.com/ScaleX-IO/vllm/blob/14d0dd92ad/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store_connector/heterogeneous_tp_cluster/run_single_node_lcm_tp4_tp2_d2.sh)

The topology matrix used the following configuration:

| Item | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Model | Qwen3-32B-FP8 |
| Hardware | One node with 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs and NVLink |
| Store transport | Mooncake standalone Store over RDMA using `mlx5_bond_0` |
| TP topologies | Prefill TP4 -> Decode TP2 and Prefill TP2 -> Decode TP1 |
| KV layouts | LBHNC -> LBHNC and LBNHC -> LBNHC |
| Functional workload | One 976-token prompt, 960 expected cached tokens, and 64 deterministic output tokens |
| Functional criteria | Store hit covers the block-aligned prefix, generated token IDs match a same-TP no-connector reference, and no Store key fails |
| Performance workload | 64 requests, concurrency 16, 64 output tokens per request, 2 warmup requests, and cold-before-cached ordering |
| Performance criteria | Every cached request hits 1,041 tokens on average, cold requests have zero cached tokens, and Mooncake reports zero failed keys |

The multiple-Prefill-TP correctness run used Prefill TP sizes 4 and 2, one
Decode TP2 instance, and common Store TP size `lcm(4, 2) = 4`. It was run once
with all endpoints using LBHNC and once with all endpoints using LBNHC. Two
distinct prefixes were written to the same layout-specific Store pool, one by
the TP4 Prefill and one by the TP2 Prefill. The same Decode instance reused
both prefixes without knowing the source Prefill TP of each request. Decode
writeback was also checked after each hit. These runs were correctness-only;
no performance claim is made from them.

## Test Result

### Unit and static checks

```text
All pre-commit hooks passed.
205 passed, 14 warnings
```

### RDMA cluster tests

All four topology/layout combinations passed functional validation:

| Prefill -> Decode | Layout | Cached / prompt tokens | Output tokens | Reference token IDs | Failed keys |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| TP4 -> TP2 | LBHNC -> LBHNC | 960 / 976 | 64 | Match | 0 |
| TP4 -> TP2 | LBNHC -> LBNHC | 960 / 976 | 64 | Match | 0 |
| TP2 -> TP1 | LBHNC -> LBHNC | 960 / 976 | 64 | Match | 0 |
| TP2 -> TP1 | LBNHC -> LBNHC | 960 / 976 | 64 | Match | 0 |

Performance results are end-to-end server measurements and include scheduling,
Store reads, KV placement, and generation.

| Prefill -> Decode | Layout | Cached req/s | Cold req/s | Throughput speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP4 -> TP2 | LBHNC -> LBHNC | 5.723 | 3.271 | 1.750x |
| TP4 -> TP2 | LBNHC -> LBNHC | 4.828 | 3.285 | 1.470x |
| TP2 -> TP1 | LBHNC -> LBHNC | 4.756 | 1.956 | 2.431x |
| TP2 -> TP1 | LBNHC -> LBNHC | 4.777 | 1.959 | 2.438x |

All runs had zero cache misses, unexpected cold hits, failed Store keys, or
connector errors.

Multiple-Prefill-TP correctness results:

For each layout, one TP2 Decode instance was connected to a single shared
Store pool containing distinct prefixes produced by both supported Prefill TP
sizes:

| Layout | Prefix | KV producer in the shared pool | Decode consumer | Decode cached / prompt tokens | Decode output tokens | Decode-writeback verification | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| LBHNC | A | TP4 Prefill | Same TP2 Decode | 1,056 / 1,057 | 64 | TP2 Prefill subsequently hit 1,104 tokens | Passed |
| LBHNC | B | TP2 Prefill | Same TP2 Decode | 1,056 / 1,057 | 64 | TP4 Prefill subsequently hit 1,104 tokens | Passed |
| LBNHC | A | TP4 Prefill | Same TP2 Decode | 1,056 / 1,057 | 64 | TP2 Prefill subsequently hit 1,104 tokens | Passed |
| LBNHC | B | TP2 Prefill | Same TP2 Decode | 1,056 / 1,057 | 64 | TP4 Prefill subsequently hit 1,104 tokens | Passed |

This demonstrates that one Decode service is not tied to a single Prefill TP
size: across requests, it can reuse KV produced by both TP4 and TP2 through the
same common Store TP size 4 namespace, without per-request source-TP metadata.
It does not mean that one request splices together KV fragments from different
Prefill executions. Mooncake reported zero failed keys and zero operation
errors.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel] Initialize NVFP4 padding in quant kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #49775 and #45739.

#45739 used a separate `torch.zeros` allocation to initialize padded NVFP4 scales. This PR moves the required initialization into the CUDA quantization kernel, allowing the wrapper to safely use `torch.empty` and avoid the extra zero-fill launch.

It also:

- Preserves a specialized fast path for unpadded output.
- Retains programmatic dependent launch support.
- Adds sentinel-based regression coverage for padded rows and columns.

This does not duplicate #47587, which covers FlashInfer’s TRT-LLM 8x4 layout. This PR targets vLLM’s built-in 128x4 swizzled kernel.

## Test Result

Validated on NVIDIA B300 with CUDA 13.4 (`sm_103a`):

- Full vLLM build passed.
- NVFP4 quantization suite: `62 passed`.
- Compute Sanitizer: `2 passed`, `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`.
- Ruff, mypy, clang-format, typos, SPDX, forbidden-import and CUDA-call hooks passed.

The benchmark results that motivated this change are documented in [the original discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49775#issuecomment-5375613975). For Llama 3.3 70B (`N=8192`, `K=28672`), the built-in 128x4 swizzled kernel shows the following before/after results:

| M | vLLM `main`, before (us) | This PR (us) | Speedup | FlashInfer CuTe-DSL (us) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.133 | 1.912 | 1.639x | 2.418 |
| 16 | 3.132 | 2.008 | 1.560x | 2.636 |
| 32 | 3.197 | 2.089 | 1.531x | 2.790 |
| 64 | 3.411 | 2.200 | 1.550x | 2.900 |
| 128 | 3.305 | 2.497 | 1.324x | 3.253 |
| 256 | 4.576 | 3.718 | 1.231x | 4.031 |
| 512 | 6.828 | 5.834 | 1.170x | 5.600 |
| 1024 | 10.791 | 9.822 | 1.099x | 9.750 |
| 2048 | 24.675 | 24.857 | 0.993x | 28.773 |
| 4096 | 46.590 | 47.080 | 0.990x | 47.462 |
| 8192 | 90.676 | 91.298 | 0.993x | 93.118 |

The change improves the launch-bound small- and medium-`M` cases by up to 1.64x and is effectively neutral at large `M`, where quantization work dominates the removed initialization overhead.

AI assistance was used to port the existing fix onto current `main`.
